# Task
Task: ajcr-charts
Title: C9 chartLocus, the chart pair, and DAT-B/DAT-C coverage
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.c9b,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.chart-u,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b; inbox=I-0492,I-0494

BUILD THE CHART LAYER: chartLocus and the (f, hf) chart pair, then close DAT-B coverage/injectivity and DAT-C Sigma-charts. Roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus (with .c9b and .chart-u) plus dat-b and dat-c. C9 is the sole gate of DAT-B B-6 AND of the whole dat-glue assembly, so this is the second-highest-leverage lane in the project.

FOUR DELIVERABLES.

 (1) CHART-U(a)/(b) — THE CO-SIGNED BRICK, and start here because nothing in the tree implements it. chartLocus c lambda (w4-datc-worksheet.md section 3.3, CHART-U(a)) is a locus over a GENERAL TEST T indexed by a plus class lambda, and isOpen_chartLocus is CHART-U(b). Its node names three missing inputs — read them before writing. This is a genuine construction task, not a proof-hunting one, and it is developable PARAMETRICALLY, i.e. without waiting for the certificate lane.

 (2) C9a IS DONE, C9b IS THE DELIVERABLE PROPER. chartLocus is already DEFINED and OPEN at the parameter-space carrier level (the C9 split of 2026-07-26). What remains is f_c, the chart morphism, and the (f, hf) pair that pic0RepresentableByOfCharts (Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) consumes. HONEST GATE, corrected and adversarially verified: c9b is NOT merely divRep-gated — read its node for what the real gate is, and note it is developable parametrically ahead of CERT-Sigma.

 (3) DAT-B COVERAGE AND INJECTIVITY: every pic^0 point is Zariski-locally a chart point. Coverage-drop, separably-closed points, divisor-family field surjectivity, local chart openness and fibre-field invariance are ALL LANDED — what remains is B5/B6/chart-locus packaging, which is exactly what (1) and (2) unblock.

 (4) DAT-C SIGMA-CHARTS: C0-C5 are landed. C6-C8 and the canonical-section certificate depend on the certificate/divRep chain — take them as far as the frozen shapes allow and say plainly where you stopped.

ONE SCARE ALREADY CLOSED, do not re-open it: the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis at Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79 is REDUNDANT, not a gap — Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130/:140 supply it as instances and the module is in the import closure (record at Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210). That file also proves Smooth => GeometricallyReduced in mathlib generality and is flagged as an upstreaming candidate.

WORKSHEET-FIRST IS THE HOUSE RULE on this lane: w4-datc-worksheet.md governs, and where a node says WORKSHEET-FIRST the worksheet section is written or updated BEFORE the Lean.

CONCURRENCY IS BINDING. Four AJCR teams at once. Follow informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md exactly: private-index compare-and-swap ledger commits (never a bare git commit), and the mkdir lake mutex at /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock (DIRECTORY lock; never flock it).

COORDINATION. You consume the divRep endpoint from ajcr-divrep and the widened DivFamZar shape from ajcr-cert-r2 — but the point of this lane is that CHART-U and C9b are developable PARAMETRICALLY in those shapes, so do not idle waiting. State your assumed shape on the AJCR conversation thread and ask them to confirm or correct it. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.
